title: Release synchronization playbook: scope gating & cut criteria for API/Console/Runtime rollout
creator: Ritika Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a compact, enforceable playbook that coordinates scope locks, cut criteria, release-note bundling, and cross-team gating signals across the Redwood API, Console, and Runtime surfaces. This ticket captures the product-managed policy, automated checks we want in CI, the stakeholder roster and handoffs, and an initial communication cadence for beta -> GA rollout windows.

Background: In prior launches we experienced drift between runtime performance targets and API docs (example: batch size behavior introduced downstream of the SDK change), which caused last-minute scope reverts and customer confusion. The playbook prioritizes deterministic signals so launch decisions are reproducible and traceable.

Goals:
- Standardize the "scope lock" moment and list of must-pass signals for any multi-surface release.
- Create minimal automated gates (smoke tests + telemetry checks) to prevent obvious regressions from flowing to GA.
- Define a single owner per release window, clear fallbacks, and a release-notes bundling process so docs + developer comms land within 24 hours of GA.
- Reduce last-minute rollbacks by surfacing cost/latency delta alarms and compatibility mismatches earlier in release pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented scope-lock checklist exists and is stored in Confluence. 2) Three automated gates are added to CI: basic API contract tests, end-to-end Console story smoke, and runtime perf smoke with token-level latency quantiles. 3) Release owner and cross-functional on-call roster listed in playbook. 4) Release-notes template and owner assigned; process to collect PR summaries and changelog entries is validated in one internal dry run. 5) Communication templates (customer-facing + internal) are available and tested.
milestones: Milestone 3: Dry-run release-note bundling and doc triage (Docs/DevRel) — 2025-03-03
Milestone 4: Cross-team signoff and publish playbook (PM/Legal/Security) — 2025-03-07
Milestone 5: First enforced gate on a small internal feature release — 2025-03-10
communication_plan: Weekly syncs: Mon 11:00 PT for core release owners (PM/ENG/DES/Docs/Support). Channel: #release-orchestration slack. Two email windows for stakeholders: pre-scope-lock announcement (T-7 days) and GA readiness summary (T-1 day). External: condensed developer-facing changelog + migration notes published to docs.redwood.ai within 24 hours of GA. All templates and PRD links are in Confluence (see links in comments).
rollout_steps: 1) T-14d: Feature freeze candidate list compiled by PM; owners tagged in ticket references.
2) T-10d: Automated smoke gate added to acceptance CI for each candidate (ENG implements trifecta: API contract, Console story, runtime perf).
3) T-7d: Scope lock decision meeting; if any must-pass gate fails, the item is marked 'cut' or 'deferred'.
4) T-3d: Release notes bundle created; Docs/DevRel review; legal/security quick scan completed.
5) T-1d: Final readiness check and publish checklist signoff by release owner.
6) GA: Push release; post-deploy telemetry monitored for 72 hours with escalation rules.
7) Postmortem: 1-week blameless review to capture lessons and update playbook.
risks: Risk: Missing perf regressions on smaller sample sizes — Mitigation: require runtime perf smoke to run on representative load (10k tokens across latencies).
Risk: Documentation drift when docs owners are overloaded — Mitigation: automated PR collection and a mandatory docs review gate.
Risk: Cross-team misalignment on severity of regressions — Mitigation: severity taxonomy defined in playbook and pre-agreed rollback thresholds.
notes: Design constraint: Console UX changes must include a documented migration path and switch flag for 2 weeks post GA (DES to propose flag behavior).
Operational note: Dedicated capacity customers must be notified separately via account managers if changes touch allocation/throughput assumptions.
Metric thresholds: example thresholds to gate on are 95th percentile latency <= baseline + 20%, token cost delta <= +10% unless pre-approved.
Related artifacts: PRD draft (Confluence) and CI gating script prototypes in GitHub under infra/release-gates.
